topic: AWS Certified Developer - Associate (DVA-C02) certification exam preparation - developing, deploying, securing, and troubleshooting applications on AWS using AWS services and SDKs, including Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, S3, IAM/Cognito, KMS, CloudFormation/SAM, the AWS CodeSuite CI/CD tools, CloudWatch, and X-Ray
exam_format: 65 questions, 130 minutes, delivered at Pearson VUE test centers or online-proctored. Multiple choice (one correct answer of four) and multiple response (two or more correct of five or more). Scaled score 100-1000 with a passing score of 720; compensatory scoring, so you do not need to pass each domain individually. AWS recommends at least one year of hands-on experience developing and maintaining applications on AWS. The certification is valid for three years. Exam fee is USD 150 (plus tax where applicable) and varies by country; present any fee as approximate and advise candidates to confirm current AWS pricing.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple response clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'; every item is a real-world development scenario asking which AWS service, SDK call, configuration, or pattern is correct - NOT term definitions
audience: Application developers, backend/cloud developers, DevOps engineers, and software engineers who build and maintain applications on AWS. AWS recommends 1+ year of hands-on experience developing on AWS plus proficiency in at least one high-level programming language (e.g., Python, JavaScript/Node.js, Java). Familiarity with the AWS SDK, CLI, core services, and application security basics is assumed. A natural developer-focused companion to the AWS Solutions Architect Associate (SAA-C04), Data Engineer (DEA-C01), Machine Learning Engineer (MLA-C01), and Security Specialty (SCS-C03) courses already in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Development with AWS Services
domains.notes: The heaviest domain. Writing application code against AWS using the SDKs: AWS Lambda (event sources, environment variables, layers, concurrency and reserved/provisioned concurrency, timeouts, packaging), Amazon API Gateway (REST and HTTP APIs, integrations, authorizers, throttling, stages), Amazon DynamoDB (partition/sort key data modeling, GSIs vs LSIs, DynamoDB Streams, DAX, capacity modes, conditional writes, transactions), Amazon S3 (SDK operations, presigned URLs, multipart upload, event notifications), and application integration (Amazon SQS - standard vs FIFO, SNS, Amazon EventBridge, AWS Step Functions). Idempotency, pagination, retries with exponential backoff and jitter, and error handling. Choosing the correct service and SDK pattern for a described application requirement.

domains.name: Security
domains.notes: Securing applications: authentication and authorization with IAM (identity-based vs resource-based policies, roles, least privilege, temporary credentials via AWS STS and AssumeRole), Amazon Cognito (user pools vs identity pools, JWT tokens, federated identities), encryption (AWS KMS, envelope encryption, S3 server-side encryption options, encryption in transit), and secrets/parameters (AWS Secrets Manager vs Systems Manager Parameter Store, rotation). Choosing the correct authentication, authorization, encryption, or secrets-management approach for a described scenario.

domains.name: Deployment
domains.notes: Preparing and deploying application code: CI/CD with the AWS developer tools (AWS CodePipeline, CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, CodeCommit, CodeArtifact), Infrastructure as Code (AWS CloudFormation templates - parameters, mappings, outputs, intrinsic functions, nested stacks, change sets; AWS SAM for serverless; awareness of the AWS CDK), and deployment strategies (in-place, blue/green, canary, rolling; Lambda versions and aliases with weighted routing; AppSpec files). AWS Elastic Beanstalk and container deployment (Amazon ECS, ECR, AWS Fargate). Choosing the correct deployment mechanism and rollout strategy for a described release requirement.

domains.name: Troubleshooting and Optimization
domains.notes: Observability, debugging, and optimization: Amazon CloudWatch (metrics, custom metrics, Logs, Logs Insights, alarms, dashboards), AWS X-Ray (traces, segments, subsegments, annotations vs metadata), and structured logging. Root-causing failures (Lambda errors and throttling, dead-letter queues, API Gateway integration errors, DynamoDB throttling/hot partitions), and optimizing for performance and cost (caching with Amazon ElastiCache and DAX, DynamoDB capacity mode selection, Lambda memory/timeout tuning, connection reuse). Diagnosing and optimizing a described running application.

extra_guidance: AWS Certified Developer - Associate (DVA-C02) is a high-volume, broadly respected associate cert and the core DEVELOPER credential in the AWS path. The exam is scenario-based - the real skill it tests is 'given this application requirement, which AWS service, SDK call, configuration, or deployment pattern is correct,' NOT memorizing definitions. This course DOES involve reading and understanding CODE at a READ-AND-UNDERSTAND level - show and explain real snippets (Python/boto3 or JavaScript/Node SDK calls, AWS CLI commands, CloudFormation/SAM YAML, IAM JSON policies, DynamoDB key designs) rather than requiring students to run a live AWS account; make that explicit. Use EXACT current AWS service names: AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, Amazon DynamoDB (GSI/LSI, DynamoDB Streams, DAX), Amazon S3 (presigned URLs, event notifications), Amazon SQS/SNS/EventBridge, AWS Step Functions, AWS IAM, AWS STS, Amazon Cognito (user pools vs identity pools), AWS KMS, AWS Secrets Manager, AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, AWS CodePipeline/CodeBuild/CodeDeploy/CodeCommit/CodeArtifact, AWS CloudFormation, AWS SAM, AWS CDK, AWS Elastic Beanstalk, Amazon ECS/ECR/AWS Fargate, Amazon CloudWatch (Logs Insights), and AWS X-Ray - with a one-line note that AWS evolves fast, so verify against current docs. The four domain names and weights above are AWS's official DVA-C02 exam-guide weights (Development 32%, Security 26%, Deployment 24%, Troubleshooting and Optimization 18%) - use them verbatim. Note the 3-year validity and the recommended 1 year of hands-on experience. Labs are READ-AND-UNDERSTAND developer walkthroughs (wire a Lambda + API Gateway + DynamoDB app, design a DynamoDB partition key and a GSI, generate an S3 presigned URL, choose SQS vs SNS vs EventBridge, set up a CodePipeline with a canary Lambda deploy, add X-Ray tracing, apply least-privilege IAM). Cover the classic DVA-C02 traps: SQS vs SNS vs EventBridge vs Step Functions, DynamoDB partition-key/hot-partition design and GSI vs LSI, Cognito user pools vs identity pools, IAM identity-based vs resource-based policies and STS AssumeRole, KMS envelope encryption, Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store, Lambda versions/aliases for canary/blue-green, CloudFormation change sets and nested stacks, and exponential backoff/idempotency. NEVER promise a pass or use the word 'guarantee' in ANY form (Udemy compliance) - use 'exam-focused preparation' framing throughout, including learning objectives and who-this-is-for. Present the exam fee as approximate (~USD 150, varies by country) and advise verifying current AWS pricing and the latest exam guide. The final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 130-minute, 65-question time-management strategy. Scan the practice bank for stray other-vendor terms (Azure/Google/NVIDIA) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
